title: Cross-Plane Automated Triage & Patch Delegation for Model Rollout Regressions
creator: Ava Chen
description: When model rollouts show regressions in production we currently rely on manual triage and ad-hoc coordination between hosted operations, Dedicated infra, and Private customer liaisons. This ticket implements an automated triage pipeline that classifies a regression signal, prioritizes affected tenants, and delegates remediation actions to the appropriate control plane (hosted, dedicated, private) with an auditable handoff. Goals: reduce mean time to safe-fallback, minimize customer blast radius, and provide a single actionable incident artifact for SRE/PM/Support.
acceptance_criteria: A signed signal from runtime (latency/regression detector) triggers the triage pipeline end-to-end in staging and production test-slices.
Pipeline correctly classifies incidents into: config/regression/model-quality/serving-runtime and recommends one of: immediate-pin, split-traffic, canary-quarantine, or emergency-rollback.

Delegation module emits a control-plane-specific remediation task with links to runbook and generated patch (hosted: route config; dedicated: autoscale/instance pin; private: customer liaison email template + patch bundle).
Audit trail created in incident store with tenant impact table and suggested rollback window.
Manual override by oncall is supported and recorded; automated remediation can be gated by customer SLA tags.
End-to-end tests that simulate a canary-quality regression in hosted, dedicated, and private environments pass in CI (integration tests exist as PRs linked).
steps: Design signal fingerprint: combine model output divergence, prompt suite failures, latency and error-rate spikes into a regression score.
Build classification model (rule + heuristics) to map regression score to remediation recommended action.
Implement delegation engine that maps remediation action -> control-plane task template and target team (ops/dedicated-ops/customer-liaison).
Integrate with rollout-service API to open a rollback/traffic-split job automatically when confidence > 0.9 and customer_impact is high.
Create audit event in incident-store with tenant slice, KV-cache reconciliation hints, and PR links for generated patches.
Wire safe-guards: rate-limits, cooldown windows, and manual approval hooks for Private deployments.
Add observability: dashboard tile for triage events, per-tenant impact heatmap, and a daily digest for PM/support.
End-to-end QA: run simulated regressions across hosted/dedicated/private slices during nightly Canary lab runs.
progress_updates: 2026-02-19 - Ava Chen: Initial discovery: aggregated dataset of 42 historical regressions collected from incident-store; identified three dominant failure modes (model-behavior drift, KV-cache mismatch after pin, and kernel scheduling degradation).

2026-02-22 - Diego Morales: POC classifier implemented (rule-based + logistic fallback) and running against replay dataset; precision 0.88, recall 0.82 for high-impact regressions. Pushed POC to infra-internal branch. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/4872)

2026-02-27 - Design review: UX for delegation artifacts reviewed with Support; created standard customer-liaison template and rollback comms copy. Drive doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-rollback-templates
2026-03-03 - Security: verified no keys are embedded in generated patches; private-control-plane delegation will surface a signed bundle for customer ingestion (security review waived for prototype).
2026-03-07 - Ops feedback: dedicated-ops requested a canary quarantine mode that leaves read-only serving capacity to help debug KV-cache state; added to remediation templates.
2026-03-11 - Integration: rollout-service API schema extended to include 'delegation_reason' and 'tenant_priority' fields. Integration tests added: runtime/integration/test_delegation.py
2026-03-12 - Current blocker: private deployment delivery requires an automated bundle signer (HSM integration) — tracking as sub-issue ENG-47210.
